home.title: Which habits are linked to a longer life
home.intro: This site covers {count} studies of food, exercise, sleep and daily habits. Each one starts with what you can do, then says how strong the evidence is and links the original papers. Where a popular claim got the numbers or the conclusion wrong, the site says so. The research summaries come from the open-source HowToLiveLonger project, which checked each claim against the original paper. This site has not changed the medical content.
home.best.title: Advice with the strongest evidence
home.best.intro: The {count} studies graded A or B where the research supports the original claim. Trials in people already diagnosed with a disease are under "{illness}" instead.
home.topics.title: Browse by topic
home.myths.title: Popular claims that do not hold up
home.myths.intro: Of the original claims, {corrected} need correcting, {partly} are only partly right and {nodirect} have no direct evidence on deaths.
home.read.title: How to read the evidence
home.read.grades: Each study has a letter grade for how direct and reliable its evidence on deaths from any cause is.
home.read.association: Most studies here are observational. They find that a habit and a lower risk of death go together, but they cannot show that the habit caused it, because age, income, smoking and other factors can affect both. Randomized controlled trials are better at showing cause and effect.
home.read.additive: Each hazard ratio compares two groups within one study. You cannot add up numbers from different studies or turn them into years of life you would gain.

about.title: About this site
about.intro: This site turns the research checks of HowToLiveLonger into pages you can read by topic. The medical content comes unchanged from that project. This site changes only how it is organized and shown.
about.method.title: Where the content comes from
about.method.text: HowToLiveLonger began as "A Programmer's Guide to Longevity", a list of longevity claims and numbers. Its reviewers later looked up each cited paper. For every claim they recorded the effect estimate, the interval, the comparison and the study population, judged whether the claim holds, and noted which part of the paper they read. {original} records come from the original guide and {added} were added during the review.
about.method.limits: This is not a systematic review. For most sources the reviewers read only the abstract. The "Original research" section of each study page says what was read. The letter grades are the project's own practical scale, not a formal GRADE assessment.

about.disclaimer.title: Not medical advice
about.disclaimer.text: This site summarizes published research to help you judge health claims. It cannot replace a clinician's judgement about your own situation. If you have symptoms, take medication or plan to change a treatment, talk to a clinician first.

about.contribute.title: How to contribute
about.contribute.text: If a number, population or conclusion is wrong, propose a change to HowToLiveLonger following {guide}. Include the original paper, the study design, the population, the comparison and the interval. After the change lands upstream, this site picks it up on the next sync.
about.contribute.site: For problems with this site's layout, interface text or translations, open an issue in this site's source repository.
